name: Elton Mill

layers.essential_history: [[c:Elton had two water mills as long ago as 1086, when the Domesday Book was written. The village's earliest manor stood close by, at Nether End beside the mill, where people have lived since Roman times.]]
layers.deeper_history: [[c:Roman pottery from the first century has been found in the parish, and the remains of the old manor site turned up during flood defence work near the mill.]]
layers.mystery: [[c:The mill wheel is still in the dark. Thomas Wade the miller swears nothing in his mill has been touched, but his own count of flour sacks doesn't add up.]]

sources.title: Elton Parish Council: A short history of Elton

directions_to_next: [[c:Head west, about 50 metres as the crow flies, to Elton Lock. The lock is a short way further on, on the river. Keep to the pavements and paths.]]

puzzle.title: [[c:The miller's sacks]]
material: [[c:THOMAS: "I had twelve sacks of flour yesterday. I sold five at market and carried four up to the loft. The rest are stacked by the wheel."]]
[[c:You count the sacks by the wheel: there are four.]]
puzzle.question: [[c:How many sacks SHOULD be by the wheel?]]
hints: [[c:Start with twelve and take away the ones that left.]]
[[c:Twelve take away five, take away four.]]
puzzle.reveal: [[c:There should be three, but there are four. Someone added an extra sack in the night.]]

evidence: [[c:An extra flour sack appeared by the mill wheel overnight.]]
